config.title: Notification Context

intro.title: Notification Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a notification system using Vue's Composition API. You will create a reusable context that manages a list of notifications, allowing any component in your app to display alerts. The core concept is using `provide` and `inject` to share state and functions across components without prop drilling. You'll implement features like adding and removing notifications, and style them with Tailwind CSS. By the end, you'll understand how to manage global state in a Vue application for user feedback.
intro.usecase: Notification contexts are essential in modern web applications where users need real-time feedback without disrupting their workflow. In e-commerce platforms like Shopify or Amazon, notification contexts manage cart updates, order confirmations, and inventory alerts that appear consistently across product pages, checkout flows, and user dashboards. SaaS applications like Slack or Trello use notification contexts to display message alerts, task assignments, and system status updates that persist across different views and components. This pattern allows developers to maintain a centralized notification system that can be accessed from any component while keeping the UI clean and user experience consistent.

objectives: Initialize a reactive notification state using Vue's ref or reactive
Construct a notification component that conditionally renders based on state
Implement a notification context provider to share state across components
Apply the notification context in child components to trigger messages
Configure notification types (e.g., success, error) with dynamic styling
Control notification visibility with automatic timeout or manual dismissal
Integrate the notification system into a Vue application structure
